questions.prompt: What is a Docker image made of?

options.text: A single compressed file with no internal structure
A stack of read-only layers, each a set of filesystem changes
A running process and its memory

questions.explanation: An image is a stack of read-only layers. Layers are shared across images and cached during builds, which saves space and time.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a tag and a digest?

options.text: A tag is immutable; a digest can change
A tag is a movable label; a digest is an immutable content hash of the exact image
They are two words for the same thing
A digest is only used for private images

questions.explanation: A tag like 1.27 or latest can be re-pointed to a new image. A digest (sha256 hash) always refers to the exact same image bytes.

questions.prompt: Why is depending on the `latest` tag risky for reproducibility?

options.text: latest is not a fixed version; it is whatever was most recently tagged, so it can change silently
latest always points to the oldest version

questions.explanation: latest is a movable label, not a version. The same reference can resolve to a different image over time, which undermines reproducibility.

questions.prompt: Docker's curated official images live in the special ______ namespace, which is why you can reference them by a bare name like nginx. (one word)
questions.explanation: Official images live in the library namespace, so nginx, library/nginx, and docker.io/library/nginx:latest all mean the same image.

questions.prompt: Which are good practices when choosing and referencing images? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pin an explicit version tag instead of relying on latest
Pin a digest when you need byte-for-byte reproducibility
Prefer official or verified base images
Always use the newest random image with the most stars, regardless of publisher

questions.explanation: Pin versions or digests and prefer trusted (official/verified) images. Popularity alone is not a substitute for checking the publisher.

questions.prompt: Match each part of docker.io/library/nginx:1.27 to what it is.
questions.explanation: A full reference is registry/namespace/repository:tag. Missing parts default to docker.io, library, and latest.
